source.title: Regularizing Neural Network Training via Identity-wise Discriminative Feature Suppression

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies the amount and type of label noise and reports test-set macro F1, a different measure from the claim’s training-error and test-error measures.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for fitting arbitrary label noise; that cited result is not this study’s evidence. The study reports test macro F1 under noisy labels, but does not report training error for these conditions.
record.test_reason: The study uses random-label memorization as motivation for ASIF and evaluates robustness through test macro F1 and noisy-label detection. It does not establish perfect fitting of corrupted training labels, fitting completely random labels, or the temporal order of learning signal and noise. Declining test macro F1 alone does not establish V4's joint memorization-and-generalization effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: ASIF can reduce overfitting and improve robustness to noisy labels, especially at high noise. Their experiments do not establish perfect training fit across the corruption sweeps. However, the broader assertion that training accuracy is never reported needs correction: Figure 2 presents training and test accuracy curves for a DGR-versus-DANN comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Adds an Identifier module and dynamic gradient reversal, changing the network and training objective; studies noisy rather than wholly random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, label-noise type and noise fraction; ASIF’s CIFAR10 instance-dependent macro F1 is non-monotonic between η 0.6 and 0.7.

fits_no_version.finding: CE and ASIF test macro F1 decrease monotonically across every recorded noise sweep; ASIF often improves robustness relative to CE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label corruption reduces test macro F1 in these experiments, while ASIF often mitigates the reduction.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 describes slower classification-loss reduction and less training/test accuracy divergence with DGR than with DANN-style reversal at 80% symmetric noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic gradient reversal reduces overfitting relative to the compared gradient-reversal method in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Table VI reports higher instance-identification loss from frozen ASIF features than from CE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ASIF features make individual training samples harder to identify with a trained linear classifier.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA 2022)
record.problems: No training-error values are reported for the noisy-label conditions. The experiments do not use wholly random labels or noise level η=1. Macro F1 is not test error; the tables show several datasets and noise types but do not establish chance-level test performance. The label-noise experiments compare different methods, including ASIF, which changes the model.
record.rows_left_out: None; all reported test macro F1 values for the label-noise sweeps in Tables II, III, X and XI are included. Other results (reduced-data F1, noisy-label detection, identifier loss and feature analysis) do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a random-corruption sweep and the accompanying test-error trajectory from clean labels to fully random labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing those regularizers.
Direct comparison over training of learning shared real-label patterns versus memorizing noisy labels; the learning-order statements are background assumptions.

record.verdict_notes: The table values in r1–r48 match the supplied text. Remove the record's V4 verdicts: the reported macro F1 sweeps do not establish the claimed fitting behavior. The alleged non-monotonic r9–r10 interval is an extraction interpretation error: 65.6 to 61.6 is a decrease. ASIF hyperparameters also vary across noise conditions in Tables VII–VIII. Statements about arbitrary-label fitting cite Zhang et al.; statements about learning general rules first do not supply a direct learning-order experiment.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, and test at chance.
Training time and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
Whether training error remains perfect; corruption up to all labels; whether test error, rather than macro F1, rises steadily toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Test macro F1 generally declines as corruption rises, as shown in r1–r48; this supports only the test-performance trend.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Macro F1 rises from η 0.6 to η 0.7, so the decline is not steady (r9–r10).
